text:
alex_w: Heads-up: us-east GPU pool at ~96% and we're seeing p95 latency spikes on long-context L models. Thinking about triggering cross-region spillover + model downgrade. Anyone else seeing this?

infra-bot: ALERT: us-east.gpu-srv queue_depth=72 p95_latency=420ms threshold=70. Auto-scale attempted: +0 nodes (capacity exhausted).

maria_g: seeing it too. us-west has spare cycles but egress out of us-east is already ~4.2Gbps; could hit bandwidth caps if we spill too much :thinking_face:. Also some AZs reporting packet drops ~0.2%.

ryan_s: we should prefer in-region model-fallback first for non-SLA tenants to avoid egress costs. idea: route by tenant_tier, then model-grade fallback chain. sample rule:```json
{"match": "tenant.tier in [\"free\", \"dev\"]", "fallback_sequence": ["gptx-small-4bit","gptx-medium-4bit","spillover-us-west"]}
```

alex_w: Proposed policy (quick):
1) admission-control: throttle tier in [free, dev] with dynamic rate limit tied to pool_utilization (eg. if pool_util > 85% -> 429 for bursty requests)
2) fallback sequence: base-4bit -> quant-small -> cross-region spill (only if fallback still queued)
3) preserve sticky affinity per-request-id for KV cache warmup where possible (avoid cold starts)
Config example:```yaml
admission:
  thresholds:
    - pool: us-east
      util_cutoff: 0.85
      actions:
        - throttle: {tiers: [free, dev], rate: "requests_per_min: 1000"}
fallback:
  sequence: ["gptx-small-4bit","gptx-medium-4bit","spillover-us-west"]
```

kyle_p: we need to be careful — model fallback changes can cause quality regressions (hallucinations) for some integrators. recommend a 2% canary + regression test suite before broad rollout, and a warmup window so caches aren't flushed mid-request.

maria_g: agree. canary 2% sounds right. alternative short-term: reduce batch size and prioritize latency SLOs for enterprise traffic, move non-critical work to background queue. smaller batch = lower throughput but helps p95.

samir_ops: rough egress cost calc for context: spilling 1M tokens from us-east -> us-west ~ 60GB egress. at $0.09/GB = ~$5.4k. If we spill sustained, cost grows fast. Suggest adding "spill_cap_per_minute" and an alert when ~80% of that cap is used.

alex_w: Action items: @maria_g add canary config (2% fallback traffic) + run short eval on fallback models; @ryan_s implement tiered admission rule + spill_cap enforcement; @samir_ops add egress-cost/spill alerts and a hard throttle if budget exceeded; @kyle_p run targeted evals and rollback criteria. I'll schedule a 10m sync if queue_depth > 80 in the next 30m.

infra-bot: Task created: "spillover-cap" alert (severity=high). Runbook: https://go/runbooks/spillover. Auto Escalation on sustained queue_depth>80 for 5m.

elaine_support: FYI CS flagged 2 enterprise customers complaining about latency for realtime features. Please ensure enterprise tier is excluded from fallback and throttles (we should route to dedicated capacity or burst pool).

alex_w: noted — enterprise excluded in the draft policy. will post the rollout plan + exact RBAC/tenant maps here once done. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
